claim: Fjäderholmarna is the closest archipelago island, reachable in about 30 minutes from central Stockholm, while Vaxholm takes around an hour.
quote: Fjäderholmarna is just 30 minutes away by boat from Stockholm, while Vaxholm can be reached in about an hour.

claim: Waxholmsbolaget and SL Commuter Boats run year-round public ferry services to inner archipelago islands; Strömma and Fjäderholmslinjen run dedicated guided/seasonal services from Strömkajen.
quote: Waxholmsbolaget offers yearly trips to many of the archipelago's gems. SL season tickets are accepted during low season.

claim: Approximate one-way ferry times and Waxholmsbolaget prices: Vaxholm 50 min / 75 SEK, Grinda 1h 20m / 150 SEK, Sandhamn 2h 10m / 170 SEK (or 360 SEK with Strömma guided tour).
quote: Vaxholm: 50 minutes each way, 75 SEK ferry or 270 SEK round-trip with commentary... Grinda: 1 hour 20 minutes each way, 150 SEK... Sandhamn: 2 hours 10 minutes each way, 170 SEK ferry or 360 SEK with guided tour.

claim: Strömma's Cinderella boats reach Grinda in roughly 1h 30m one-way for ~230 SEK, departing Strandvägen.
quote: Strömma (Cinderellabåtarna): Takes 1 hour 30 minutes one way and costs 230 SEK

claim: Sandhamn via Cinderella boats takes about 2.5 hours from Strandvägen berth 14, with tickets from SEK 255 and stops at Nacka Strand, Vaxholm, Grinda and Gällnö en route.
quote: To Sandhamn: from SEK 255... The Sandhamn route departs from Strandvägen, berth no 14 in Stockholm and makes multiple stops along the archipelago route including Nacka Strand, Vaxholm, Grinda, Gällnö

claim: Utö is far out — fastest practical route is commuter train to Västerhaninge + bus 846 to Årsta Brygga then ferry (~35 min–1 h); summer-only direct Waxholmsbolaget service runs from Strömkajen taking ~3h 58m one-way.
quote: Utö can be easily reached by boat from both Nynäshamn, Årsta Brygga and in summertime also from Strömkajen at the Grand Hotel in Stockholm.

claim: Drottningholm Palace boat trip on Lake Mälaren takes 50–60 minutes from Klara Mälarstrand aboard M/S Prins Carl Philip, with returns at SEK 220 / one-way SEK 170 (kids 6–15 half price, under-6 free).
quote: Ferry tickets cost SEK 220 for adults (return) or SEK 170 (one-way), with children ages 6-15 at half price and under-6 free.

claim: Stockholm's Open Electric (open-top) sightseeing boat is a 50-minute eco-friendly guided harbour tour rated 4.8/5 across 658 reviews, departing near the Gustav III statue.
quote: The Guided City Sightseeing Open Electric Boat Tour has a rating of 4.8 out of 5 stars with 658 reviews.

claim: Central-Stockholm kayak rentals (SUPKAJAK, Långholmen Kajak, Lek Mer at Smedsudden/Pampas, plus self-service ShareKayak/Kayakomat) operate through summer; Skärgårdens kanotcenter in Vaxholm is the standard archipelago base.
quote: Skärgårdens kanotcenter (Vaxholm; rentals up to two weeks)... ShareKayak and Kayakomat operate stations throughout Stockholm with online/app booking.

claim: Beginner-friendly Vaxholm-based small-group kayak tours (max 8 people, stable double kayaks, paddle/jacket/dry-bag included) run 4-hour fika-stop trips or 6-hour BBQ versions.
quote: Small-group tours are limited to eight people or fewer, include paddles, life jackets, kayaks, and waterproof bags... use stable double kayaks, with single kayaks available on request.

claim: Vaxholm Fortress cable-ferry runs mid-May to mid-September with 2–4 trips per hour and an 80 SEK ticket; Vaxholm itself works as a walking-and-fika town with colourful wooden houses.
quote: The Vaxholm castle ferry operates mid-May to mid-September and runs 2-4 trips an hour. Vaxholm castle tickets cost 80 SEK.

claim: Fjäderholmarna's seasonal businesses (brewery, smokery, craft studios) reopen in early May 2026, making late-May a good time; ferries depart Slussen, Strömkajen and Strandvägen berth 13 with Waxholmsbolaget fares SEK 61–186.
quote: Waxholmsbolaget (public ferries) range from "SEK 61 to SEK 186" depending on distance... closed for the season with reopening stated for early May 2026
